clue.text: Lover's lost love in European capital

indicators.note: the lover has lost something, so a letter drops out of his name

parts.note: Romeo is the archetypal lover, from Shakespeare
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic loses his sweetheart while visiting a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Lover's lost' as 'Lover has lost': ROMEO without one O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital city of Italy, a European nation.

clue.text: Flinch in fear on bend

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in business letters
a coil is a bend or loop of rope or wire

explanation.surface: Someone shies away nervously at a sharp turn in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to draw back suddenly, a synonym for shrinking away from something frightening.

clue.text: Bodyguard died in pit on top of ridge

indicators.note: the abbreviation for died is placed within the word for pit

parts.note: a mine is a pit dug for coal
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter, so only the start of ridge is used

parts.note: first letter of ridge

explanation.surface: A protector died in a mine shaft at the top of a hill ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside MINE to give MINDE; 'top of' takes R, the first letter of ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A minder is British slang for a personal protector or heavy, as in the TV series of that name.

clue.text: Leaders, real idiots, in dissaray

indicators.note: in disarray (misspelt so in the clue) means jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Political leaders, being real idiots, are in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like politicians, but here it means newspaper leading articles; 'in dissaray' (sic) jumbles the letters of 'real idiots'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader in British newspapers is the main opinion column, also called an editorial.

clue.text: Sister in party dress can

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a mini is a short dress
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nun, wearing a party dress, holds a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sister is a nun, and a Dominican is a nun of the order founded by St Dominic.

clue.text: What some northerners eat is rubbish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cow's stomach lining, traditionally eaten in northern England
second meaning: nonsense or worthless stuff

explanation.walkthrough: Tripe, the edible stomach lining of cattle, is a traditional dish in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The offal sense names a food; the slang sense calls something worthless nonsense.

clue.text: Reading this may get one over sin, might we deduce?

definitions.text: Reading this may get one over sin, might we deduce?

parts.words: Reading this may get one over sin, might we deduce?
parts.note: a Bible translation helps a reader overcome sin, and the letters of 'over sin' are themselves a reworked form of the second word

explanation.surface: Studying a certain text might help someone triumph over wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Revised Version is an 1880s English Bible. 'Over sin' is a rearrangement of VERSION, so it is literally a revised version of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Revised Version is a well-known English translation of the Bible, the scripture read to overcome sin.

clue.text: Cooked, covered with breadcrumbs, I turn Aga off

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone switches off the Aga cooker once the crumb-topped dish is done.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy British range cooker. 'off' looks like switching it off but signals rearranging 'I turn Aga'.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes a dish browned under a topping of breadcrumbs or grated cheese.

clue.text: Tapes wound round small garden plant

indicators.note: the rearranged tapes go around the word for small
wound (past of wind) suggests twisted, so the letters of tapes are rearranged

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Tapes are tied around a little plant in the garden for support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' rearranges tapes to STPEA, which goes 'round' WEE, the Scottish word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a fragrant climbing flower commonly grown in gardens.

clue.text: Favouritism in the workplace that does not extend to girls?

definitions.text: Favouritism in the workplace that does not extend to girls?

parts.words: Favouritism in the workplace that does not extend to girls?
parts.note: the idiom for posts handed to friends and insiders is read literally as work reserved for males

explanation.surface: Office favouritism seems to exclude women.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes cronyism, giving positions to friends or allies rather than on merit.

clue.text: Agree to study mould

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a form is a mould into which something is shaped

explanation.surface: Someone consents to examine a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform with something is to comply or be in accord, a synonym of agreement.

clue.text: I name magazine that's current

parts.note: Vogue is a famous fashion magazine

explanation.surface: Someone names a magazine that is up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue is fashionable right now, popular at the present time.

clue.text: Substantially surrounded by German city church

parts.note: being surrounded by something is being in it
Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church is enclosed by the buildings of a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: In essence means fundamentally or basically, matching the adverb for in substance.

clue.text: Celebrity, first in training to jump

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: only the opening letter of training is used

parts.note: first letter of training

explanation.surface: A famous athlete, first in training, leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to give a sudden jerk or jolt from surprise.

clue.text: Extremely happy, nun once idol destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun once destroyed an idol and was overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being blissfully elated, floating with delight.

clue.text: Bulbs kept initially in paper

parts.note: onions are bulbs

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of kept

parts.note: first letter of kept

explanation.surface: Bulbs are stored, wrapped in paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Onionskin is a thin, translucent writing paper, named for its resemblance to an onion's skin.

clue.text: Old copper writes down eye specialists

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to list things is to write them down

explanation.surface: An elderly policeman takes notes about eye doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculists are doctors or practitioners who treat or test eyes.

clue.text: Flares up over recently stolen photograph

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first part sits above the second

parts.note: to snap is to lose one's temper suddenly
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone explodes in anger over a stolen picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly.

clue.text: Stable in eastern walled city

parts.note: constant means steady or stable

explanation.surface: A stable stands inside an eastern walled city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' looks like a building for horses, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantine is an ancient fortified city in north-eastern Algeria, perched on a rocky plateau.

clue.text: Horrified at hag's concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at a witch's brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock or dismay, a synonym for appalled.

clue.text: Prison camp over in Bengal, at Siliguri

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means flipped upward, so the letters are read in reverse
the answer is held in these words, across their joins

parts.note: the letters G-A-L-A-T-S run across the end of Bengal, the word at and the start of Siliguri

explanation.surface: A prison camp turns up in Bengal, at the town of Siliguri.
explanation.walkthrough: Siliguri is a city in West Bengal, India. 'in' finds GALATS inside the words, and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.

clue.text: Decline drinks, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a cat laps, or drinks with its tongue

explanation.surface: Someone refuses drinks, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline drinks' reads as turning down a round; 'say' is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a falling-off or decline in standards or behaviour.

clue.text: Thinking back, criminal hid things

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Looking back, a crook concealed possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is understanding an event after it has happened, the view from looking backward.

clue.text: Muscular dog

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an Arctic sled dog

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves as both an adjective for a brawny build and the name of a sled-pulling breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Husky means big and strong in build, and a husky is a sturdy Arctic sled dog.

clue.text: Check on fatality by entrance to Stormont Castle

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Stormont is used

parts.note: first letter of Stormont
CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a loss is a death, as in loss of life

explanation.surface: A security check after a death at the gate of Stormont, the Northern Ireland parliament building.
explanation.walkthrough: Stormont is the seat of the Northern Ireland Assembly in Belfast; 'entrance to' takes its first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Schloss is the German word for a castle or palace, used in English for such buildings.

clue.text: Cocky type rounded hill, was almost captured

indicators.note: captured means held inside, so the shortened word goes into the hill

parts.note: a knoll is a small rounded hill

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A cocky person was nearly caught on a rounded hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from 'was' to leave WA, and 'captured' places WA inside the hill word; the hyphenated answer is a common British term.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a conceited person who thinks they know everything.

clue.text: Cool enough?

parts.note: cool in its slang sense of good or fine, and enough in its sense of sufficing, together describe being pleasing and adequate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like temperature, but it is the approving slang sense: good and adequate together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfying is pleasing and sufficient, meeting needs or expectations.

clue.text: Male part shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a stage is a part or phase of a process

explanation.surface: The man's role was cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male part' reads as a man's role, but 'Male' alone is the definition; 'shortened' drops the final E of STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and the word also means male-only, as in a stag party.
